finish() in lib/driver.sh (around line 519) queues the driver's own continuation with `bin/harness queue add --continue <run> --keep-attempts`; cmd_continue (bin/harness:212-217) skips a `--queued` continuation when `ended` starts with `stopped by Michael`. R6 must leave that call automatic while `harness queue add --continue` typed by Michael marks `--requested`. queue_add (bin/harness:108-113) numbers from `ls $Q` only; `park` (bin/harness:306-310) is a plain mv into $Q/held/. control() in lib/driver.sh:165-170 reads INBOX.md's `status:` line with a `stop*` prefix match, so `status: stop <reason>` already stops; cmd_control (bin/harness:321-328) only touches $st/STOP. summary.mjs derives end_reason and feature causes from `ended`: check its matching when the string grows a suffix.

The stub claude (tests/stub-claude.sh) acts on the prompt's first line and STUB_* env flags (STUB_PHONE_STOP=1 writes `status: stop` to INBOX.md through a clone of the origin; STUB_STRICT_VERIFIER, STUB_THIN_VERIFY, STUB_LENIENT, STUB_NO_TAMPER, STUB_NO_RED). Its initializer writes a fixed list A, B (M1) and C (M2; STUB_INDEPENDENT_M2=1 gives C `after: []`) with steps x, y, z, so lint will report findings in every stub run: assert counts, not clean. Every new flag goes in the stub's header comment.

R5's deterministic scenario: the driver's loop checks `n >= MAX_SESSIONS` before verify_ready, so a config with MAX_SESSIONS=2 ends a stub run `session cap (2)` right after B passes, M1 complete and unverified; `harness continue <run> --until-epoch $(( $(date +%s) - 1 )) --foreground` then hits `deadline reached` at the loop top (run 9c and the scrub section already use --until-epoch in the past). No timing-based test needed.

The full suite takes ~600 s on this box (10 min under check.sh); the Bash tool's foreground limit is 600 s. Run it in the background or with a longer timeout, and iterate on a scratch copy of the one section you are adding to (the lifecycle run did: copy the preamble, lines 1-58, plus your section to /tmp and run that).

lib/features.mjs is pure functions plus a main() dispatch; a new command goes in the usage header comment at the top and in the `default:` usage line. Unit checks in tests/run.sh use `node --input-type=module -e` importing from lib/features.mjs (see the `the scheduler, pure` section). Prompt variables are rendered by lib/prompt.sh (prompt_vars/prompt_env); bin/harness passes HARNESS_* overrides to tmux-started drivers from an explicit list in cmd_start: add any new HARNESS_* variable there.

header:
# Progress — run `agent-harness-2026-10-26-2` (agent-harness)

What this file is: the run's journal, rendered from `entries.jsonl` after every session, newest entry first (the full record is `progress-archive.md`; the driver's own notes are `harness-log.md`). Each entry says what one session did, what passed, what it found (discoveries) and what it needs from you (questions).

The spec is `docs/specs/2026-10-21-retro-fixes.md`, scoped by the brief to F1 and F2 (F3 is subsumed by lanes). F1 · driver and CLI correctness: real test counts (R1), verify never trusts the suite cache (R4), requested continuations run (R6), a stop records why (R7), queue numbering and park refusal (R11). F2 · initializer and verify: reviews sized to the milestone (R2), step lint at init (R3), the initializer's `after` line (R10 change 2), one verify before the deadline (R5). The two milestones are independent: a stuck feature in one never blocks the other. Each verified milestone merges into `main` by itself.

How to read the feature list: `feature_list.json` lists features in priority order; `passes` is the session's claim, the verify entry for a milestone is what counts. Steps are the checks a verifier re-runs. Each build feature writes its checks first (in the `# ---- <title> ----` section of `tests/run.sh` that matches its topic, or the `tests/checks/` file if the suite split has landed), its decision file under `journal/decisions/`, and its `docs/architecture.md` and `README.md` lines.

To steer: edit `INBOX.md` on this branch (GitHub app). Line 1 `status: pause` or `status: stop` takes effect before the next session; answers go under `## Answers`. Sessions never park on this run (the brief): they take the spec's default and record it in the decision file, so the questions below are for after the run.
